Released: 21 September 2026


!!!Warning PGD-S is no longer accepted
PGD-S (PGD Essential) is no longer offered as a product. `tpaexec configure --architecture PGD-S` now fails immediately, as does `reconfigure`/`provision`/`deploy` against an existing cluster whose `config.yml` still specifies `architecture: PGD-S`. Use PGD-X for new PGD 6 deployments.
!!!

!!!Warning Potential restart of Postgres on first deploy
On clusters where `max_wal_senders` and `max_replication_slots` are set only under `postgres_conf_settings` (not directly as `cluster_vars`), upgrading to 23.45.0 may restart Postgres once, if TPA's recalculated value differs from the value previously written to `conf.d/0001-tpa_restart.conf`. Setting both variables directly as `cluster_vars`, in the same deploy as the upgrade, avoids this.
!!!

New features, enhancements, bug fixes, and other changes in Trusted Postgres Architect 23.45.0 include the following:

## Highlights

- Split sysctl management into separate vm and network groups, so a routine deploy no longer resets operator-tuned network settings
- Added support for running the TPA controller on, and experimentally deploying to, Debian 13 (trixie)
- PGD-S (PGD Essential) is no longer accepted by tpaexec configure; use PGD-X instead

## Enhancements

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now splits its sysctl management into separate vm and network task groups.</summary><hr/><p>TPA used to write a single mixed set of sysctls into <code>/etc/sysctl.conf</code>,
combining Postgres-specific kernel tuning (the <code>vm.dirty_*</code> family,
<code>vm.zone_reclaim_mode</code>) with general-purpose network and connection tuning
(<code>net.core.somaxconn</code>, <code>net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog</code>, and others). A
routine <code>tpaexec deploy</code> could silently reset network values that an
operator had raised on purpose to handle their workload, which has caused
production incidents.</p>
<p>TPA now splits these settings into two task selectors. <code>sysctl_vm</code>
covers the Postgres-specific group and is applied by default; exclude
it with <code>excluded_tasks: [sysctl_vm]</code> to manage those settings yourself.
<code>sysctl_net</code> covers the network group and is opt-in only, via a new
<code>opt_in_tasks</code> mechanism: <code>tpaexec configure --platform aws</code> opts the
cluster in by default, while bare-metal and other platforms stay opted
out unless <code>sysctl_net</code> is added to <code>opt_in_tasks</code>. The settings are
written to <code>/etc/sysctl.d/30-tpa.conf</code> rather than <code>/etc/sysctl.conf</code>, so
an operator's own file under <code>/etc/sysctl.d/</code> with a higher numeric
prefix (for example <code>/etc/sysctl.d/90-local.conf</code>) takes precedence
through the standard Linux mechanism, without going through
<code>config.yml</code>.</p>
<p><code>opt_in_tasks</code> is a new third task-selector list (alongside
<code>included_tasks</code> and <code>excluded_tasks</code>) for tasks that should run only
when explicitly opted in. Unlike <code>included_tasks</code>, it does not engage
whitelist semantics: naming a task in <code>opt_in_tasks</code> opts that task in
without implicitly excluding any other tasks.</p>
<p>The historical network defaults have also been audited against current
Linux kernel defaults. <code>net.core.somaxconn</code>, <code>net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies</code>,
and <code>net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse</code> are no longer set by TPA, since the kernel
defaults are now the values TPA wanted. <code>net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range</code>
has been narrowed at the bottom end so it no longer overlaps the
privileged-port range.</p>
<p>On the first redeploy under the new layout, TPA also removes any of its
historical sysctl lines from <code>/etc/sysctl.conf</code>, so the two files don't
end up shadowing each other.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports running the controller on Debian 13.</summary><hr/><p>The TPA controller can now be a system running Debian 13 (&quot;trixie&quot;),
either from a source checkout (using the system Python 3.13 packages)
or via <code>apt-get install tpaexec</code>, now that tpaexec packages are
published for Debian 13.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports experimental deployment to Debian 13 (trixie) nodes.</summary><hr/><p>TPA can now deploy to nodes running Debian 13 (&quot;trixie&quot;). Suitable
Docker images or AWS AMIs are selected on the docker or aws platforms,
and <code>bare</code> instances running Debian 13 are detected correctly.</p>
<p>This feature is experimental: deployment depends on the availability
of the various packages for Debian 13, so not all architectures or
software options will work until packages are uploaded to upstream
repositories.</p>
<p>Debian 12 remains the default Debian version, so existing clusters and
any new cluster configured without an explicit <code>--os-version</code> are
unaffected.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports preserving ansible.log across deprovision instead of deleting it.</summary><hr/><p><code>tpaexec deprovision</code> always deleted the cluster directory's
<code>ansible.log</code> along with other generated files. Setting
<code>preserve_ansible_log: true</code> at the top level of <code>config.yml</code> now
preserves it instead: the current log is renamed to <code>ansible.log.N</code>,
one more than the highest existing suffix, leaving earlier logs under
their original names. This is useful when repeatedly provisioning and
deprovisioning the same cluster directory during development. Default
behavior is unchanged.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports controlling the startup of the Postgres service when EFM is the failover manager.</summary><hr/><p>A new variable, <code>efm_autostart_db</code>, controls whether the Postgres
service starts automatically after EFM starts when EFM is used as the
failover manager. It defaults to <code>false</code>; set it to <code>true</code> to have
Postgres start automatically once EFM starts.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now provides an Echo (Debian-based) execution environment variant for AAP 2.4.</summary><hr/><p>A new <code>echo</code> execution-environment base is available under
<code>tpa-ee/aap24/echo/</code>, built on <code>reg.echohq.com/python:3.12-slim</code>
(&quot;Echo Linux&quot;, a Debian derivative). It's an alternative to the
existing <code>alpine</code> variant for users who need an apt-based, glibc image.
Build it the same way as the other variants: <code>build.sh -b echo</code>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports the <code>pgaa</code> extension.</summary><hr/><p>The <code>pgaa</code> extension can now be installed by TPA when listed in the
extensions list. <code>pgaa</code> requires <code>pgfs</code> as a prerequisite; TPA checks
for the presence of <code>pgfs</code> when <code>pgaa</code> is listed, to avoid failing
later in the deployment.</p>
<p>To check the list of supported platforms and Postgres versions, see
https://www.enterprisedb.com/docs/pgaa/latest/overview/compatibility/.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now repeats its deliberate warnings in a recap at the end of a run.</summary><hr/><p>Warnings that TPA raises on purpose to draw the operator's attention
were printed only inline as a run proceeded, where they could scroll
out of sight during a long deploy. TPA's output now collects those
deliberate warnings and repeats them in a consolidated block after the
PLAY RECAP, so they are not missed. Warnings emitted by Ansible itself
are left out of this recap, so it stays focused on the messages TPA
chose to raise.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports the <code>pgfs</code> extension.</summary><hr/><p>The <code>pgfs</code> extension can now be installed by TPA when listed in the
<code>extra_postgres_extensions</code> list.</p>
<p>To check the list of supported platforms and Postgres versions, see
https://www.enterprisedb.com/docs/pg_extensions/pgfs/compatibility/.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now supports EFM 5.4's <code>primary.health.check.port</code> property.</summary><hr/><p>EFM 5.4 adds a new property, <code>primary.health.check.port</code>, that load
balancers can use to locate the primary node in a cluster. When set, an
EFM agent listens on that port for incoming HTTP requests: the primary
agent responds with a 200 status code, and other agents respond with a
404.</p>
<p>TPA now supports setting this property in <code>efm_conf_settings</code>; it is
ignored if set while deploying a version of EFM before 5.4.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Changes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>TPA now requires <code>--pgd-proxy-routing</code> to be specified when reconfiguring a BDR4 cluster to PGD5.</summary><hr/><p>When reconfiguring a BDR4 cluster to PGD5, <code>--pgd-proxy-routing</code> must
now be set to <code>global</code> or <code>local</code>. This is enforced consistently for
<code>--describe</code>, <code>--check</code>, and a real run, so an omitted or invalid value
is now reported immediately instead of only being caught partway
through the process.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th><th width="10%">Addresses</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby recalculating max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots could trigger an unnecessary Postgres restart.</summary><hr/><p>TPA calculates its own defaults for <code>max_replication_slots</code> and
<code>max_wal_senders</code> on every deploy and writes them to
<code>conf.d/0001-tpa_restart.conf</code>, even on clusters where these settings
are actually governed by <code>postgres_conf_settings</code> (which takes
priority over any other value). Because the calculation formula for
<code>max_replication_slots</code> has changed across recent TPA versions (to
account for PGD 5 Parallel Apply), upgrading TPA could change the value
written to <code>conf.d/0001-tpa_restart.conf</code> and trigger a Postgres
restart, even when the values actually in effect (from
<code>postgres_conf_settings</code>) never changed.</p>
<p>TPA now validates that <code>max_wal_senders</code> is at least as large as
<code>max_replication_slots</code>, failing deployment with an explanatory error
instead of silently adjusting either value as before. A new
<code>skip_wal_senders_validation</code> variable is available as a temporary
escape hatch for clusters transitioning an existing, inconsistent
configuration.</p>
<p>To avoid the restart described above, set <code>max_replication_slots</code> and
<code>max_wal_senders</code> directly as <code>cluster_vars</code> with the value you want in
effect, rather than only under <code>postgres_conf_settings</code>.</p>
<p>See the warning at the top of these release notes: upgrading to this
version may still restart Postgres once if these variables are only
set under <code>postgres_conf_settings</code>.</p>
</details></td><td>65323</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby BDR/PGD clusters on Postgres 16 and later could suffer a permanent Raft consensus failure on first startup.</summary><hr/><p>Postgres 16 added <code>output_plugin_libraries</code>, an allow-list GUC that
rejects any output plugin not named in it (default: <code>pgoutput, test_decoding</code>). BDR/PGD's consensus worker uses the <code>bdr</code> library
itself as an output plugin, so on any build where this GUC exists and
doesn't already allow <code>bdr</code>, the consensus worker crashed at first
startup. That happened during the cluster's very first boot, while
Raft was still bootstrapping, permanently stranding that node with no
Raft leader: every later <code>bdr.create_node_group()</code> call then failed
with &quot;could not establish consensus leader&quot;, and the deploy failed.</p>
<p>TPA now adds <code>bdr</code> to <code>output_plugin_libraries</code> before Postgres ever
starts, on any build that supports the GUC, so the consensus worker
never crashes in the first place.</p>
<p>TPA also now retries BDR node group creation on transient consensus
errors, as a defensive measure independent of the above.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby pgd-proxy could fail to connect to Postgres because libpq environment variables were not passed to its systemd service.</summary><hr/><p>The <code>pgd-proxy</code> service is started by systemd, which does not pass a
user's ambient environment through to spawned services. As a result,
<code>pgd-proxy</code> could fail to connect to Postgres when it relied on libpq
environment variables, such as <code>PGPASSFILE</code>, that were not present in
the service's environment.</p>
<p>TPA now sets these variables directly in the <code>pgd-proxy</code> systemd unit
file via a new <code>pgd_proxy_service_environment</code> variable, which defaults
to:</p>
<pre><code>pgd_proxy_service_environment:
  PGPASSFILE: '&#123;&#123; pgd_proxy_home }}/.pgpass'
  PGSSLMODE: 'require'
</code></pre>
<p>Each entry is rendered as an <code>Environment=</code> line in the unit file. You
can override the variable under <code>cluster_vars</code> or a pgd-proxy
instance's <code>vars</code> to change or add environment variables; the value you
supply replaces the default mapping in full rather than being merged
entry by entry.</p>
</details></td><td>61496, 63632</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby every deploy logged a spurious Ansible warning that the raw module does not support the environment keyword.</summary><hr/><p>The task that records the deploy in the log file inherited a
play-level environment it never used. It is now given an empty
environment, so the spurious warning no longer appears. This is purely
cosmetic; deployment behavior is unchanged.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby PEM server nodes were given a fixed node name instead of a generated one.</summary><hr/><p>PEM server nodes created with <code>--enable-pem</code> were always given the
fixed name <code>pemserver</code>, instead of a generated name consistent with the
naming scheme used by the rest of the cluster. This also prevented
them from receiving a generated hostname via <code>--hostnames-from</code>. PEM
server nodes now receive a generated node name and hostname like other
nodes in the cluster.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby changes to the pgd-proxy systemd unit file were not applied on redeploy.</summary><hr/><p>Changes to the <code>pgd-proxy</code> systemd unit file (for example, editing
<code>pgd_proxy_service_environment</code>) were written to disk but did not take
effect on the running service when re-running <code>tpaexec deploy</code> on an
existing cluster: the role restarted the service without first running
<code>systemctl daemon-reload</code>, so systemd kept using its cached unit, and a
change confined to the unit file did not trigger a restart at all.</p>
<p>TPA now reloads systemd and restarts <code>pgd-proxy</code> whenever the unit file
changes, so unit-file settings are applied on redeploy as expected.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby <code>efm_bind_by_hostname</code> was silently reset during EFM switchover and upgrade health checks.</summary><hr/><p>When a cluster was configured with <code>--efm-bind-by-hostname</code>, EFM
switchover (<code>tpaexec switchover</code>, and the EFM switchover step used
mid-upgrade by <code>tpaexec upgrade</code>) and the EFM health checks run around
<code>tpaexec upgrade</code>/<code>tpaexec upgrade-efm</code> incorrectly used the node's IP
address instead of its hostname to identify itself when querying <code>efm cluster-status-json</code>. Both task files unconditionally reloaded EFM's
role defaults (including <code>efm_bind_by_hostname: false</code>) over the
user-configured value, silently reverting the cluster to IP-based
identification. As a result, tasks that look up a node by its EFM
identity (<code>efm set-priority</code>, cluster-status polling, and the &quot;node is
part of allowed nodes&quot; check) could fail on clusters configured with
<code>--efm-bind-by-hostname</code>.</p>
<p>The role defaults are now only used as a fallback for variables that
are not already defined, so a user-configured <code>efm_bind_by_hostname</code>
(and <code>efm_cluster_status_retries</code>/<code>efm_cluster_status_retry_delay</code>, if
overridden) is preserved.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby the Patroni rewind user lacked the privileges pg_rewind needs.</summary><hr/><p>The Patroni rewind user (<code>patroni_rewind_user</code>, default <code>rewind</code>) was
created as a plain non-superuser role with no privileges, so the first
<code>pg_rewind</code> Patroni attempted after a failover failed with &quot;permission
denied for function pg_read_binary_file&quot;, leaving the demoted primary
unable to rejoin the cluster as a replica.</p>
<p>This fix grants the rewind user EXECUTE on the three pg_catalog
functions pg_rewind requires (<code>pg_ls_dir</code>, <code>pg_stat_file</code>,
<code>pg_read_binary_file</code>), matching what Patroni itself grants during
bootstrap. Re-running <code>tpaexec deploy</code> on an existing cluster applies
the fix.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby Patroni REST API test and management calls could fail under mTLS with a non-root SSH user.</summary><hr/><p>Calls to Patroni's REST API, used by <code>tpaexec test</code> and by
switchover/restart management operations, could fail with a
permission-denied connection error when the cluster used mTLS
authentication for the API and the connecting SSH user was not root -
the recommended configuration on AWS and bare metal. This no longer
happens.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby a pgbouncer/pgd-proxy port clash on the read-only port went undetected.</summary><hr/><p>TPA already stopped a deploy if pgbouncer and pgd-proxy were both
configured to listen on the same port on the same host, but it only
checked the main (read-write) port. If the clash was instead on
pgd-proxy's read-only port, TPA didn't notice, and one of the two
services could quietly fail to start.</p>
<p>Deploy now checks both ports for a clash, and fails with a clear
message, instead of stopping abruptly with a confusing error, if
pgd-proxy's listen port isn't set in <code>config.yml</code> at all.</p>
<p>Deploy also now stops with a clear message if a host runs pgd-proxy
but its read-only port (<code>read_listen_port</code>) isn't set. When
<code>bdr_package_version</code> isn't set in <code>config.yml</code>, TPA assumes BDR 5.5 or
later, which needs this port, so it requires <code>read_listen_port</code> rather
than letting pgd-proxy start without read-only routing.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby pgd-cli was installed but not configured on proxy nodes during a BDR 4 to PGD 5 upgrade.</summary><hr/><p>A BDR-Always-ON to PGD-Always-ON major upgrade (BDR 4 to PGD 5)
converts dedicated harp-proxy nodes into pgd-proxy nodes, which require
pgd-cli. The upgrade installed the pgd-cli package on those nodes but
never wrote its configuration file, leaving pgd-cli present but
unusable there (<code>/etc/edb/pgd-cli/pgd-cli-config.yml</code> was absent). The
upgrade reported success regardless, so the problem was silent.</p>
<p>TPA now writes the pgd-cli configuration on those nodes during the
upgrade, so pgd-cli is fully installed and configured on the new
pgd-proxy nodes.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby pgd-cli authentication failed on dedicated pgd-proxy nodes.</summary><hr/><p>On a dedicated pgd-proxy node (one with no postgres/bdr role), pgd-cli
was configured with endpoints that connect as the Postgres superuser,
but the node's <code>.pgpass</code> holds only the pgd-proxy user's password. As a
result, pgd-cli could not authenticate against any endpoint and failed
with <code>fe_sendauth: no password supplied</code>.</p>
<p>TPA now sets each pgd-cli endpoint to connect as the user appropriate
to the node running pgd-cli, the pgd-proxy user on dedicated pgd-proxy
nodes, so pgd-cli works out of the box there. Postgres and BDR nodes
are unaffected.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby the psycopg2 canary test failed on clusters with a non-root login user.</summary><hr/><p><code>tpaexec test</code> aborted at &quot;Install psycopg2 import canary script&quot; with
&quot;Destination /etc/tpa not writable&quot; on any cluster whose <code>ansible_user</code>
is not root, such as a typical AWS or bare-metal cluster. The test now
installs and removes its canary script with the privileges it
requires, so the psycopg2 import check runs as intended regardless of
the login user.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby Barman package installation failed on Debian/Ubuntu for Barman 3.20 and later.</summary><hr/><p>Since Barman 3.20.0, installing from EDB's own repository on Debian or
Ubuntu ships Barman's Python client library under a new package name,
<code>edb-python312-barman</code>, instead of <code>python3-barman</code>. TPA now selects
the correct package name automatically, so deployments and upgrades to
Barman 3.20 or later succeed on Debian and Ubuntu when using EDB's
repositories. Installs from the PGDG repository, and all RedHat/SUSE
installs, are unaffected.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby TPA's generated ssh_config prevented Ansible Tower's own SSH credential from being used.</summary><hr/><p>When a cluster is managed by Ansible Tower, TPA no longer writes an
<code>IdentityFile</code> or <code>IdentitiesOnly</code> setting into the cluster's
<code>ssh_config</code>. Tower supplies the SSH key through its own machine
credential, and pinning TPA's own key here prevented that credential
from being used, which forced operators to override
<code>ansible_ssh_common_args</code> by hand after every provision.</p>
<p>The generated <code>ssh_config</code> still sets the connection port, the
cluster's <code>known_hosts</code> files, and <code>ServerAliveInterval</code>, so Tower
clusters now get the correct SSH behavior out of the box with no
manual editing. Clusters that are not managed by Tower are unaffected.</p>
</details></td><td>61496</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby a HARP cluster could become unroutable after a re-deploy.</summary><hr/><p>TPA now re-applies the HARP cluster bootstrap configuration when the
consensus store (DCS) has lost it, not only when the on-disk bootstrap
file has changed. Previously, if the DCS was emptied or re-provisioned,
or an initial bootstrap was interrupted, while the bootstrap file was
left unchanged, a re-deploy would silently skip re-applying it and
leave HARP-proxy unable to route connections.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby tpaexec upgrade --components=pg-backup-api was a silent no-op.</summary><hr/><p>Upgrading pg-backup-api via <code>tpaexec upgrade --components=pg-backup-api</code>
did nothing unless a specific package version was pinned in
<code>config.yml</code>, even when a newer version was available. It now upgrades
to the latest available version by default, matching barman,
pgbouncer, and PEM.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby redeploying could reset the certificate ownership of a TLS-using service colocated with Postgres.</summary><hr/><p>Redeploying a cluster where a TLS-using service (for example etcd)
shared a node with Postgres could leave that service's certificate and
CA files owned by the Postgres system user instead of the service's
own user, breaking TLS for that service until the files were manually
fixed. This no longer happens.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby the pkg-config package was missing from the required package list for Debian-based systems.</summary><hr/><p>The <code>pkg-config</code> package was missing from the list of required
packages for Debian-based systems, causing build failures when
compiling software that relies on it. <code>pkg-config</code> has been added to
the list of required packages, so builds from source now proceed
without errors related to this missing dependency.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby tpaexec switchover failed on EFM clusters.</summary><hr/><p><code>tpaexec switchover</code> on a cluster with <code>failover_manager: efm</code> no
longer fails after promotion with a &quot;requested handler ... was not
found&quot; error while regenerating EFM configuration for the new
topology.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby M1 deploys failed when efm tasks were excluded.</summary><hr/><p>Deploying an M1 cluster configured with <code>--enable-efm</code> using <code>tpaexec deploy --excluded-tasks=efm</code> failed on the primary with &quot;Role
'efm_role' does not exist&quot;: the task granting privileges to
<code>efm_role</code> did not honor the task selector, while the tasks that create
the role did. The grant tasks are now skipped along with the rest of
the efm tasks. In addition, the replication user's <code>.pgpass</code> entry was
only written by the (excluded) efm role, leaving <code>pg_basebackup</code>
waiting forever for a password when cloning the replica; the entry is
now written regardless of the task selector.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby upgrading pem-agent with update_hosts could fail when restricted to a subset of hosts.</summary><hr/><p>Upgrading the pem-agent component with <code>update_hosts</code> restricted to a
subset of hosts could fail with an undefined-variable error on any PEM
agent host excluded from that subset. The restart step now only runs
against the hosts actually being upgraded.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby enabling pg-backup-api without PEM or beacon-agent produced a configuration with no EDB repository enabled.</summary><hr/><p>pg-backup-api is only published to EDB's Cloudsmith repositories, never
to PGDG. Configuring a community-Postgres cluster with
<code>--enable-pg-backup-api</code> (without <code>--enable-pem</code> or
<code>--enable-beacon-agent</code>) previously produced a <code>config.yml</code> with an
empty <code>edb_repositories</code> list, so the generated configuration could not
install pg-backup-api. TPA now enables the standard EDB repository
whenever <code>--enable-pg-backup-api</code> is used, matching the existing
behavior for <code>--enable-pem</code> and <code>--enable-beacon-agent</code>.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby PGD-X/PGD-S minor version upgrades could fail spuriously on clusters using non-default Connection Manager ports.</summary><hr/><p>The listening-ports check run during PGD-X/PGD-S minor version upgrades
always checked the generic default Connection Manager ports instead of
the ports actually configured for the cluster's node group, causing the
check to fail with a connection error on any cluster that configures
non-default <code>read_write_port</code>/<code>read_only_port</code> values.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby Postgres user and role DDL could fail during BDR3/BDR4-to-PGD5 or PGD5-to-PGD6 major version upgrades.</summary><hr/><p>During a BDR3-to-PGD5, BDR4-to-PGD5, or PGD5-to-PGD6 (PGD-X) major
version upgrade, TPA could run Postgres user and role DDL (creating
users, granting roles) on a node immediately after restarting it,
before BDR Raft consensus had stabilized and before the node was
unfenced. This could cause replicated DDL to fail with errors such as
&quot;failed to get a DDL epoch&quot; or &quot;consensus request timed out&quot;.</p>
<p>TPA now waits for Raft consensus to stabilize before running this DDL,
and only unfences the node afterwards, matching the correct sequence:
fence, stop/update/restart Postgres, wait for consensus, run DDL,
unfence.</p>
</details></td><td>61496</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby PostgreSQL could be installed from the OS repository instead of PGDG/EDB on RHEL, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, CentOS Stream, and Oracle Linux 10.</summary><hr/><p>On RHEL, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, CentOS Stream, and Oracle Linux 10, the
OS BaseOS/AppStream repositories ship their own PostgreSQL packages.
Because DNF modularity, which TPA previously relied on to keep the OS
repositories from providing PostgreSQL, was removed in these EL10
distributions, TPA could end up installing PostgreSQL from the OS
repository instead of PGDG or EDB. The OS package's systemd unit is
named differently from the one TPA expects, so deployment then failed
while trying to manage the PostgreSQL service.</p>
<p>TPA now excludes PostgreSQL, Barman, and repmgr packages from the OS
BaseOS and AppStream repositories on all of these EL10 distributions,
so PostgreSQL is always installed from PGDG or EDB as intended. This
matches the exclusion behavior already in place for earlier RHEL
family versions (7, 8, and 9, which rely on DNF module exclusion).</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby the Patroni readiness check could give up early despite its retry budget.</summary><hr/><p>The wait for a Patroni node to report itself ready during deploy,
switchover, and <code>tpaexec test</code> could abandon its 3-minute retry budget
after only a few seconds, causing spurious failures on nodes whose
Patroni API was simply slow to start listening. When the wait does
fail, TPA now includes a recent excerpt of Patroni's own log in the
error, making the underlying cause visible without logging in to the
node.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby newly generated cluster CAs lacked an X509v3 Key Usage extension.</summary><hr/><p>TPA's generated cluster CA carried no X509v3 Key Usage extension.
Python 3.13 enables strict X.509 verification by default, and strict
verification rejects a CA certificate with no keyUsage extension at
all, so any Python TLS client running on a node with Python 3.13 or
newer (for example Debian 13) and verifying against TPA's CA would
fail, even though the CA itself was otherwise valid.</p>
<p>This fix adds the required keyUsage extension to newly generated CAs.
Existing clusters are not affected: a CA already on disk keeps working
exactly as before and is never regenerated by this change. If you later
need a fixed CA for an existing cluster (for example, before adding a
node running Python 3.13 or newer), delete <code>&lt;cluster_dir&gt;/ssl/CA.crt</code>
(keep <code>CA.key</code>) and redeploy to have it re-signed with the new
extension.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby Connection Manager ports were not applied correctly when local routing was enabled.</summary><hr/><p>PGD reads the Connection Manager options (<code>read_write_port</code>,
<code>read_only_port</code>, <code>http_port</code>, and <code>use_https</code>) only from the node
group that has routing enabled. With <code>--pgd-routing local</code> that is each
location subgroup, but <code>tpaexec configure</code> wrote the ports to the
top-level group, where they had no effect: Connection Manager silently
fell back to listening on <code>postgres_port + 1000</code> and
<code>postgres_port + 1001</code> instead of the requested ports.</p>
<p><code>tpaexec configure</code> now places these options on the location subgroups
when local routing is selected, and on the top-level group when global
routing is selected. Existing clusters do not need their <code>config.yml</code>
edited: a routing-enabled subgroup that does not set these options
itself now inherits them from its parent group, so redeploying moves
Connection Manager onto the configured ports.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed an issue whereby update_hosts scoping could cause PGD5-to-PGD6 and PGD6 minor upgrades to fail or skip proxy downtime monitoring.</summary><hr/><p>Several plays in the PGD5-to-PGD6 major upgrade and PGD6 minor upgrade
playbooks were incorrectly scoped to the <code>update_hosts</code> subset when
they actually depend on cluster-wide state (the connection manager
endpoint for every node, and write-leader detection). This caused
upgrades to fail or silently skip proxy downtime monitoring whenever
<code>update_hosts</code> was used to upgrade a subset of hosts that excluded the
cluster's current primary or write leader. These plays now always run
across the whole cluster, regardless of <code>update_hosts</code>.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Deprecations

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>PGD-S is no longer accepted as an architecture at configure time.</summary><hr/><p>PGD-S (PGD Essential) is no longer offered as a product. <code>tpaexec configure --architecture PGD-S</code> now fails immediately with a clear
error instead of creating a cluster. The same check applies to
<code>tpaexec reconfigure</code> and <code>tpaexec provision</code>/<code>deploy</code> against an
existing cluster whose <code>config.yml</code> still specifies <code>architecture: PGD-S</code>. Use PGD-X for new PGD 6 deployments instead.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
